1 خَدَبَهُ , (S, K,) aor.
خَدُبَ , inf. n. خَدْبٌ, (TA,) He smote him with a sword: (S, K:) or he cut him: (AZ:) or he smote him with a sword, cutting the flesh, without cutting the bone: (T, K:) or he smote him on the head, (JK, K, * TA,) and the like, (JK, TA,) with a sword. (JK.) ―
-b2- خَدْبٌ signifies also The act of rending, or cutting open, the skin and the flesh together, (JK, S, TA.) with the canine tooth. (JK, TA.) ―
-b3- And The act of biting. (K.) You say, خَدَبَتْهُ الحَيَّةُ The serpent bit him. (S.) ―
-b4- And The act of lying, or saying what is untrue. (K.) You say, خَدَبَ He lied. (JK, S.) ―
-b5- And The act of milking much. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
